newsitem.title: USA: Centrum Inds CEO sees FY98 earnings growth.
newsitem.headline: Centrum Inds CEO sees FY98 earnings growth.

text.p: Centrum Industries Inc Chief Executive Geroge Wells said he expects to double pre-tax profits and revenue in fiscal 1998 through acquisitions.

In fiscal 1998 ending March 31, "we should double the $1.7 million in earnings projected for fiscal 1997 and our sales should be in the mid-$80 million range," Wells said in an interview with Reuters on Friday.
Wells said the company hopes to attain a Nasdaq listing this year, noting, "We have to get the price up a bit, but we meet all of the other criteria -- capital, shares outstanding and net worth."
Centrum Industries is a holding company with three businesses. One, Micafil Inc, is a maker of production machinery for fractional horsepower motors.

Its American Handling unit is a provider of material handling systems and components used in warehouses and the third unit, McInnes Steel Co, is a provider of specialty steel forgings for the power generation and compressor industries.
Wells said Centrum will continue to look to acquire underperforming companies in its niche markets and make them profitable by trimming costs and improving distribution quality.
"We would like to buy one company every 10 to 12 months," Wells said. "Our goal is to acquire one additional company in 1998, we are now looking at two or three candidates.
He said every acquisition the company has made so far has had a positive effect on the company's earnings.
Centrum is looking to expand the size of its future acquisitions into the $30 million plus range, Wells said. Previously, most of its acquisitions were in the $5-20 million range.
"It costs as much to look at a $5-10 million company as a $30 million company," he noted.
